name: Question 8
problem:
Let $f(x,y,z)$ be a differentiable function such that

$$
f(3,3,1)=3,\,{f}_{x}(x,y,z)=\frac{yz}{2\sqrt{xyz}},\,{f}_{y}(x,y,z)=\frac{xz}{2\sqrt{xyz}},\,{f}_{z}(x,y,z)=\frac{xy}{2\sqrt{xyz}}.
$$

Using a linear approximation of $f$ at the point $(3,3,1),$ estimate the value of $f(3.01,3.02,0.98).$
worked_solution:
The linear approximation of the function $f$ at the point $(a,b,c)$ is given by

$$
f(x,y,z)≈f(a,b,c)+∇f(a,b,c)\cdot ⟨x-a,y-b,z-c⟩.
$$

So, the linear approximation of $f$ at the point $(2,-2,-1)$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x,y,z) & ≈f(3,3,1)+∇f(3,3,1)\cdot ⟨x-3,y-3,z-1⟩ \\  & ≈3+⟨{f}_{x}(3,3,1),{f}_{y}(3,3,1),{f}_{z}(3,3,1)⟩\cdot ⟨x-3,y-3,z-1⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we find ${f}_{x}(3,3,1)$, ${f}_{y}(3,3,1)$ and ${f}_{z}(3,3,1),$ using the given partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{x}(3,3,1) & =\frac{(3)(1)}{2\sqrt{(3)(3)(1)}}=\frac{1}{2} \\ {f}_{y}(3,3,1) & =\frac{(3)(1)}{2\sqrt{(3)(3)(1)}}=\frac{1}{2} \\ {f}_{z}(3,3,1) & =\frac{(3)(3)}{2\sqrt{(3)(3)(1)}}=\frac{3}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
f(x,y,z)≈3+⟨\frac{1}{2},\frac{1}{2},\frac{3}{2}⟩\cdot ⟨x-3,y-3,z-1⟩.
$$

Finally, we can estimate $f(3.01,3.02,0.98)$ by evaluating the linear approximation at $x=3.01,y=3.02$ and $z=0.98,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(3.01,3.02,0.98) & ≈3+⟨\frac{1}{2},\frac{1}{2},\frac{3}{2}⟩\cdot ⟨3.01-3,3.02-3,0.98-1⟩ \\  & ≈3+⟨\frac{1}{2},\frac{1}{2},\frac{3}{2}⟩\cdot ⟨0.01,0.02,-0.02⟩ \\  & ≈3+(0.005+0.01-0.03) \\  & ≈2.985\end{aligned}
$$

Using a linear approximation of f at the point (3,3,1), estimate the value of f(3.01,3.02,0.98).

b

c
 3.070
d

Correct
EXPLANATION

The linear approximation of the function f at the point (a,b,c) is given by f(x,y,z)≈f(a,b,c)+∇f(a,b,c)⋅⟨x−a,y−b,z−c⟩.

So, the linear approximation of f at the point (2,−2,−1) is f(x,y,z)≈f(3,3,1)+∇f(3,3,1)⋅⟨x−3,y−3,z−1⟩≈3+⟨fx(3,3,1),fy(3,3,1),fz(3,3,1)⟩⋅⟨x−3,y−3,z−1⟩.

Now, we find fx(3,3,1), fy(3,3,1) and fz(3,3,1), using the given partial derivatives: fx(3,3,1)=(3)(1)2(3)(3)(1)=12fy(3,3,1)=(3)(1)2(3)(3)(1)=12fz(3,3,1)=(3)(3)2(3)(3)(1)=32

Therefore, we have f(x,y,z)≈3+⟨12,12,32⟩⋅⟨x−3,y−3,z−1⟩.

Finally, we can estimate f(3.01,3.02,0.98) by evaluating the linear approximation at x=3.01,y=3.02 and z=0.98, as follows: f(3.01,3.02,0.98)≈3+⟨12,12,32⟩⋅⟨3.01−3,3.02−3,0.98−1⟩≈3+⟨12,12,32⟩⋅⟨0.01,0.02,−0.02⟩≈3+(0.005+0.01−0.03)≈2.985
